info.title: Pocketmark HTTP API
info.description: Native API for your personal bookmark library. JSON errors have an error field. Browser requests use the existing owner session automatically; integrations send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Named keys cannot manage the account, API keys or full backups. First-run setup, login and health are public. Mutations enforce same-origin browser checks; configure POCKETMARK_ORIGIN to the exact public origin behind a reverse proxy. Limits measured in bytes are UTF-8 byte limits, not character counts. At most eight concurrent library requests; excess work returns 503. “Try it out” performs real operations on this instance. WebDAV /dav/ and removed Linkwarden compatibility routes are outside this reference. Public authentication has two separate slots and a five-second POST body deadline. /healthz has separate readiness slots; /livez checks process liveness independently. All HTTP requests except GET/HEAD health probes share a per-client token bucket: 10 requests/second, burst 100 by default (POCKETMARK_RATE_LIMIT and POCKETMARK_RATE_BURST). IPv6 clients share a /64. Rejection occurs before authentication/body reads and returns 429 with Retry-After. At most 256 sources are tracked; new sources fail closed at capacity. State resets on restart. Trusted forwarding requires POCKETMARK_TRUSTED_PROXIES.

requestBody.description: 4 KiB JSON limit. Only username/password are accepted; tokens cannot log in.

post.description: Password authentication only. Ten validly formed attempts per minute per client address (IPv6 /64), with at most 256 tracked sources. Excess sources fail closed. One password derivation at a time; busy callers receive 429 with Retry-After: 1. Forwarded client addresses require explicitly trusted proxy CIDRs. Sessions expire after seven days; at most 32 sessions, oldest evicted at capacity.
Revokes the current session in SQLite and clears its cookie. Revocation survives restart. Other sessions and API keys remain valid.

patch.summary: Rename, disable or reactivate an API key
patch.description: Owner only: a signed-in owner session or administrative recovery bearer token is required. Named API keys receive 403. Disabling blocks subsequent API and WebDAV authentication; reactivation restores access with the same key. Revoked keys cannot be reactivated. Supply name, active, or both. Renaming preserves the credential, creation date and usage history and does not reactivate a disabled key.

name.description: 1–120 UTF-8 bytes after trimming; changes only the display name.

Alphabetical order grouped by A–Z, followed by # for other initials. Groups contain distinct tag counts across all matching pages.

parameters.description: Jump to the first matching tag under A–Z or #. Encode # as %23. The response reports the resolved page.

get.description: Authenticated inline preview. HTML retains embedded styles/images/fonts in an opaque sandbox; scripts and network resources are blocked, refresh and external links are disabled. Original downloads remain unchanged. PDF uses the browser native viewer. Preparation shares the archive work slot.

bearerAuth.description: Paste a dedicated API key without the Bearer prefix. Named keys have library access only. Account/key management and backups require the owner session or administrative recovery token. Authorization is not persisted across reloads.

example.error: invalid JSON or request too large

401.description: Missing or invalid session or bearer credential.

403.description: Rejected browser origin or operation restricted to the owner.

404.description: Record or capture not found, or bookmark currently processing.

409.description: A conflicting operation is in progress, setup is unavailable, or the key limit was reached.

413.description: The HTML attachment exceeds the reader’s 2 MiB input limit.

example.error: rich reader accepts HTML up to 2 MiB; download the larger archive

415.description: Unsupported content type. JSON operations require application/json.

429.description: HTTP client rate limit or source-table capacity exceeded, login rate limit exceeded, or password worker busy. Retry-After indicates the retry delay in whole seconds. General rate-limit rejections include Cache-Control: no-store.

503.description: Server busy (eight library slots, two authentication slots or two readiness slots), database unavailable, or session persistence failed.
